text.p: Exxon Corp said Thursday it has filed with the U.S. District Court in Anchorage, Alaska, appealing that court's $5.058 billion amended final judgment in the Valdez case entered on Jan 17.
"We believe that this judgment should be set aside or substantially reduced," Exxon said in a statement.

It said the filing "marks the start of Exxon's appeal of this excessive and unwarranted judgement" arising from the grounding of the tanker Valdez in Prince Georges Sound nearly six years ago -- on Good Friday 1989.
Papers filed with the Anchorage court Wednesday list more than 40 substantive legal issues that may be raised by Exxon, the company said.

Exxon said it asks the Appellate Court to review the standards applied by the District Court for punitive damages under maritime law and under the due process clause of the Constitution, including a review of the size of the award.

The list of issues also includes the court's instructions to the jury, the court's requiring of a $6.75 billion letter of credit and the calculation of a number of compensatory damage awards, the company said.
It said the appeal will be heard by the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco.
